neighbours.label: clause opener (if / whether / that / what) in first-person narration, at the point where the narrator's own 'I' is the expected next word
fire: When I walked into the party late, I wondered what everyone would say if I admitted I had simply forgotten.
My boss kept staring at me, and I could not tell whether I had made a mistake or done something right.
I felt sick all morning because I was afraid that I would forget my lines on stage.
My friends laugh at me whenever I mention it, and sometimes I ask myself whether I should keep quiet.
I begged my brother to phone the school and tell them that I was too ill to sit the exam.
Nobody noticed me in the corner, so I wondered what would happen if I just slipped out the back.
I was terrified of the dentist, and I asked my mum what she would do if I refused to open my mouth.
My hands were shaking so badly that I doubted whether I could even sign my own name.
quiet: When the guests walked into the party late, the host wondered what everyone would say about the cold food.
The manager kept staring at the screen, and nobody could tell whether the system had failed or recovered.
The actors felt sick all morning because the director was afraid that the lights would fail on stage.
Her friends laugh at the story whenever she mentions it, and sometimes they ask whether the dog was real.
The boy begged his brother to phone the school and tell them that the bus had broken down.
Nobody noticed the cat in the corner, so the children wondered what would happen if the door stayed open.
The patients were terrified of the dentist, and the nurse asked what they would do if the drill was quiet.
The clerk's hands were shaking so badly that the customers doubted whether the form was signed properly.

notes: Card: top examples peak on ' think', ' that', ' saying', ' until', ' fast' right before 'I'; output promotes ' I', ' my', ' me'. Probes: first-person 0.62/0.41/0.22, same sentence in third person singular 0.24, plural or noun subjects 0.01-0.04. Near misses are the same kinds of sentences told about other people.
